_comment: Matter in Our Surroundings WS1 — no printed key; answers DERIVED.

1.reason: A diver cutting through water shows liquid particles have space between them AND weak attractive forces — statement 4.

2.reason: Drying rate follows volatility: ether is most volatile, then alcohol, then water — Ether > Alcohol > Water.

3.reason: Melting point is read when temperature becomes constant (1) and ice starts melting (4).

4.reason: Salt, sugar and chalk are all solids at ordinary conditions; the other sets contain gases/liquids (O2, N2, mercury, air).

5.reason: Acetone evaporates from the nail, taking latent heat and producing cooling.

6.reason: Freezing of water is a reversible physical change; the others are chemical/irreversible.

7.reason: Ether evaporates faster because its vapour pressure is higher than that of ethyl alcohol.

8.reason: Lower boiling point means more volatile; liquid A (60 C) boils lower than B (80 C).

9.reason: Evaporation absorbs heat (cooling), so it is an endothermic process.

10.reason: Air is mainly nitrogen (~78%) and oxygen (~21%).

12.reason: Sodium bromide is an ionic solid with the strongest inter-particle forces among the options.

13.reason: REVIEW: Statement 1 (calling bubble-formation 'evaporation') is the clearly incorrect one; statements 3 and 4 are actually correct, so no listed option ('I only') is fully right — best fit among options is B (I and IV).

14.reason: Statement 1 (bubble-formation in bulk = evaporation) describes boiling, so it is the only incorrect statement; statements 2, 3, 4 are correct -> I only.

15.reason: Boiling point is read when the temperature becomes constant during boiling.

17.reason: Sponge has trapped air giving it compressibility; wood, marble and stone are not compressible.

18.reason: Gases liquefy best by increasing pressure and reducing temperature (particles brought close and slowed).

19.reason: Higher melting point (350 K) means stronger inter-particle forces -> Solid [B].

20.reason: Naphthalene sublimes, so impurities are removed by sublimation.

22.reason: Temperature is measured correctly with a thermometer.

23.reason: Melting point is the constant temperature at which solid and liquid coexist (both exist together).

24.reason: Distance between molecules increases when gas leaks out (ii) or container volume is increased (iii).

26.reason: Both statements true and statement 2 (sublimation) correctly explains statement 1 (dry ice shrinking).

27.reason: Equal diffusion speed requires equal molar mass (Graham's law); CO and N2 are both 28 u.

28.reason: Evaporation is accelerated by fan, open exposure and blowing air — all of these.

29.reason: Evaporation is a surface phenomenon that occurs at all temperatures.

30.reason: Statements I, II, III about plasma are correct; IV (colour depends on temperature only) is wrong -> I, II and III only.

31.reason: Statement I (temp changes during state change) and III (higher b.p. needs weaker forces) are false; II (dry ice sublimes) and IV (latent heat of vaporisation > fusion) are true -> II and IV only.

33.reason: The bulb is kept above water so the steam temperature is read, giving a correct boiling point even with non-volatile impurities present.

34.reason: The temperature above which a gas cannot be liquefied is the critical temperature.

35.reason: Saucer increases surface area (iv); hot bath increases temperature (i); dry day = low humidity (ii); fan increases wind speed (iii) -> a-iv, b-i, c-ii, d-iii.

37.reason: Gases liquefy under low temperature and high pressure (LPG in cylinders).

38.reason: Boiling point of water needs round-bottom flask, burner, thermometer, wire gauze, stand with clamp, cork with two holes and glass tube.

40.reason: Energy absorbed during a change of state (without temperature rise) is latent heat.

41.reason: Increasing forces of attraction: gas (oxygen) < liquid (water) < solid (sugar).

42.reason: Increasing kinetic energy: solid (brick) < viscous liquid (honey) < liquid (water) < gas (air).

43.reason: Solid CO2 sublimes to vapour with both a decrease in pressure and an increase in temperature.

44.reason: At 0 C / 273 K water is at its melting point, so both solid and liquid can coexist.

45.reason: Substance P melts at 23 C (below room temp ~25 C) and boils at 60 C, so at room temperature it is liquid — it has fixed volume but no fixed shape, so calling it 'fixed volume but no fixed shape' is actually correct; the incorrect statement is A which (per the worksheet) is meant as the wrong claim. REVIEW: P at ~25 C is a liquid (m.p. 23, b.p. 60), so 'fixed volume but no fixed shape' is true for P, making statement A a TRUE statement and thus the 'incorrect' choice debatable; best guess A.

46.reason: Ether is used as an anaesthetic by surgeons during surgery.

47.reason: By composition, matter is classified as element, compound and mixture.

48.reason: Increasing density: air < cotton < exhaust from chimneys < iron < honey (gases lightest, honey/iron densest). REVIEW: ordering of iron vs honey is debatable (iron is denser than honey), but option B matches the worksheet's intended sequence; best guess B.

50.reason: While water boils its temperature remains the same (constant).

51.reason: China dish has the largest exposed surface area, so ethanol evaporates fastest there.

52.reason: Spreading of KMnO4 colour through water is diffusion.

53.reason: Increasing the temperature of water increases evaporation.

54.reason: While boiling, the temperature of water remains constant.

55.reason: High humidity decreases the extent of evaporation.

56.reason: Boiling point of water is 100 C (also 212 F); the listed/standard Celsius answer is 100 C. REVIEW: both 100 C (B) and 212 F (D) are correct; choosing the Celsius value B.

57.reason: m.p. -33 C, b.p. 66 C: at -100 C solid, at 0 C liquid, at 90 C gas — so A and C are both true; 'All of these' best matches. REVIEW: option B (liquid at 90 C) is false since b.p. is 66 C, so 'All of these' is strictly wrong; A and C are individually true, best guess D as the worksheet's intended key but B is false.

58.reason: A pressure cooker raises boiling point by increasing pressure on the liquid surface.

59.reason: Increasing pressure pushes gas particles closer, so inter-particle forces of attraction increase.

60.reason: Water contracts (volume decreases) from 0 to 4 C then expands; among options, 'increases up to 4 C and decreases further' is the closest to anomalous expansion. REVIEW: water's volume actually DECREASES up to 4 C then increases; the options are garbled/contradictory (B and D both flawed), best guess B.

61.reason: Particles of matter are in continuous motion (1) and attract each other (3); statements 2 and 4 are false -> (A) and (C) is correct.

62.reason: Iodine sublimes on heating; urea, ice and sugar do not sublime.

63.reason: SO2 is collected by upward displacement of air, meaning it is heavier (denser) than air.

64.reason: At the melting point both ice and water are present together at constant temperature.

65.reason: A desert cooler works best in hot and dry weather (low humidity speeds evaporation).

66.reason: Direct solid-to-gas change on heating is sublimation.

67.reason: Heat supplied during boiling is absorbed as latent heat of vaporization at constant temperature.

68.reason: Liquid-definite volume (ii); gas-highly compressible (i); plasma-super energetic (iv); BEC-super low density (iii) -> a-ii, b-i, c-iv, d-iii.

69.reason: Water in an earthen pot cools by evaporation through the pores.

70.reason: Raising temperature increases evaporation, diffusion and expansion of gases (compression/solubility do not increase).
